Job Description 
 
 About the Role: 

 Our IT team operates as a business partner proposing ideas and innovative solutions that enable new organizational capabilities. We collaborate internationally to deliver the services and solutions that help R&D global users to be more productive and enable innovation.

 A GenAI Software Engineer on our Data Science team builds the AI services that draft regulatory documents from clinical study data, and understands the product and the business well enough to know what good looks like. This is the module where clinical results become regulatory-ready narrative: you will work on the services that orchestrate model calls, ground generated text in the correct study data, and return section-level content to our authoring applications — and you will work with the authors, product owners, and data scientists who depend on that content to understand why it matters and how to make it better.

 We are building an engineer who works across the whole problem, not one layer of it. Day to day that means backend services and APIs, clinical data pipelines, AWS deployment, and applied GenAI, grounded in a real understanding of the users and the regulatory process they work within. AI is part of how we do that work: we expect you to use AI tools to learn faster, move across disciplines, and take on responsibilities that would once have required a larger team — and to bring a critical eye to when AI output is right and when it is not.

 This is a durable role on the team rather than a role scoped to a single project. Our GenAI authoring work is currently proving itself out, and our portfolio of regulatory and clinical digital solutions will keep evolving. Whatever the trajectory of any one initiative, the capabilities this role builds — backend services, clinical data engineering, cloud, product thinking, and applied GenAI in a regulated environment — are ones we will continue to invest in, and we expect the role to grow into broader responsibility alongside them.

 Key Responsibilities: 

 Product & Business Understanding: 

 Develop a good understanding of our company's biopharmaceutical R&D business processes, systems, and data, with a focus on clinical and regulatory processes.
 Learn how regulatory documents are authored, reviewed, and submitted, and use that understanding to shape what you build and how you prioritize it.
 Partner directly with product managers, medical writers, statisticians, data scientists, and business technology partners to turn user needs into well-defined technical work.
 Contribute to product discovery and refinement: ask the questions that clarify the problem, weigh options, and help define what success looks like and how it will be measured.
 Gather user feedback on generated content and translate it into concrete improvements to prompts, data, and services.
 
 GenAI Solution Development: 

 Develop, test, and maintain services that generate section-level content for regulatory documents, and extend them as new document sections and document types are onboarded.
 Design and refine LLM-based generation approaches — prompt and instruction design, structured output, grounding in source data, and guardrails — to improve the accuracy, consistency, and safety of generated regulatory text.
 Evaluate generated output rigorously: build curated test sets, define quantitative and rubric-based measures of quality, run regression comparisons as models and approaches change, and use error analysis to turn subjective quality feedback into repeatable checks.
 Work on retrieval and grounding approaches (semantic search, embeddings, vector stores) as the platform adopts them.
 Keep generated content traceable to the source data and the approach that produced it.
 Implement and refine the mapping between clinical result tables (tables, listings, figures) and the document sections they ground, including the endpoint and study metadata joins those mappings depend on.
 
 Data Engineering: 

 Work with clinical study data: read, reshape, validate, and join study metadata, endpoint lists, and result-table inventories.
 Support and extend our data pipeline — acquisition from enterprise sources, mapping calculation, document conversion, and publication to cloud storage for the application to read.
 Write validation and reconciliation logic so data problems surface as clear errors rather than as quietly wrong generated text.
 
 Backend & Platform Engineering: 

 Build and consume REST APIs that connect the Data Science services to the authoring platform, and keep those contracts stable and documented.
 Debug and resolve defects across the full request path — API input, data retrieval, prompt assembly, model response, and the content returned to the author.
 Gain working exposure to the front end and authoring surfaces so you can reason about the product end to end, from the clinical data through to the document the author sees.
 
 Cloud & Deployment (AWS): 

 Build, deploy, and operate services on AWS — S3, Lambda, ECS, RDS/PostgreSQL, Secrets Manager, and CloudWatch.
 Run services locally with Docker and ship them through our GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines.
 Contribute to Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform) for the resources your services depend on.
 Use logs, metrics, and monitoring to investigate and resolve issues in deployed environments.
 
 Testing & Quality Assurance: 

 Write unit and integration tests for the code you deliver; treat coverage of your own work as part of the definition of done.
 Participate in code reviews, both as author and as reviewer.
 Uphold quality gates in the pipeline — static analysis, security scanning, and dependency checks.
 Work within GxP and validated-system expectations: traceability, documented changes, and controlled releases.
 
 AI-Augmented Engineering: 

 Use AI coding assistants and agents as a daily part of how you design, build, test, debug, and document — and develop sound judgment about where they accelerate the work and where they need verification.
 Use AI to move across disciplines: to get productive quickly in an unfamiliar service, data model, or part of the stack, and to take on work beyond a single specialty.
 Share what works — prompts, workflows, and techniques — with the team, and help establish good practice for building with AI in a regulated environment.
 Stay current on LLM and AI tooling, and bring prototypes and informed opinions back to the squad.
 
 Collaboration & Agile Development: 

 Work in an Agile squad (Scrum/Kanban): sprint planning, stand-ups, refinement, code reviews, and retrospectives, with teammates across global time zones.
 Document your work clearly — pull request descriptions, runbooks, and module documentation that let the rest of the team pick up what you build.
 Contribute to a culture of curiosity, learning, building, and experimentation, and take on progressively broader technical scope as you grow.
 
 Education: 

 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, Data Science, Computer Engineering, or any Technology stream, or equivalent relevant experience.
 
 Required Qualifications and Skills: 

 Experience: 

 2-3 years of professional software development experience, with the level (R1 or R2) set to the depth the successful candidate brings.
 For candidates with professional experience: at least one shipped application or service you can speak to in depth, including the decisions and trade-offs behind it.
 For candidates earlier in their experience: internships, co-ops, apprenticeships, or substantial academic, open-source, or portfolio work are all relevant.
 
 Programming fundamentals: 

 Proficiency in at least one object-oriented language — Python, Java, C#, C++, or TypeScript — with a working understanding of OOP fundamentals: classes and interfaces, composition, encapsulation, and separation of concerns.
 Ability to read an unfamiliar codebase and make a correct, well-scoped change in it.
 Working knowledge of Python, or clear evidence of being able to become productive in it quickly.
 Comfort with data structures, algorithms, and debugging — able to reason about why code behaves the way it does, not just whether it runs.
 Proficiency with Git and collaborative development workflows (branching, pull requests, code review).
 SQL and an understanding of relational data modelling.
 Familiarity with REST APIs and the HTTP request/response model.
 Experience writing automated tests (pytest, JUnit, Jest, or equivalent).
 
 Cloud and AI: 

 Experience with AWS, or clear evidence of self-directed progress toward it — coursework, labs, certification in progress, or a project you have deployed to the cloud — along with the appetite to go deeper quickly.
 Hands-on experience with generative AI and LLMs: calling an LLM API, building with an AI framework, prompt design, or equivalent coursework or project work.
 Regular use of AI tools in your own development workflow, and a thoughtful view on how to use them well.
 
 Ways of working: 

 A growth mindset. You seek feedback, act on it, and treat "I don't know that yet — here's how I'd find out" as the right answer. This is the most important attribute for this role.
 Curiosity about the product and the business: you want to understand who uses what you build, what problem it solves for them, and how to tell whether it is working.
 Analytical and detail-oriented, with care for correctness — in this domain, a plausible but wrong sentence is a defect, not a rounding error.
 Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to work comfortably with both technical and non-technical partners; able to ask good questions early and raise blockers without being asked.
 Able to work independently on well-scoped problems and collaboratively on ambiguous ones.
 Legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future. (Adjust per TA guidance.) 
 
 Preferred Qualifications and Skills: 

 Hands-on AWS experience across S3, Lambda, ECS/Fargate, RDS, IAM, Secrets Manager, and CloudWatch.
 AWS certification (Cloud Practitioner, Developer Associate, Solutions Architect Associate) — held or in progress.
 Experience with LLM APIs (Anthropic Claude, Amazon Bedrock, OpenAI), including exposure to RAG, embeddings, vector databases, or prompt evaluation approaches.
 Python data work with pandas, numpy, or openpyxl, and experience wrangling CSV- and Excel-shaped data.
 Backend API development with FastAPI, Flask, Django, Express, or Spring.
 Experience building, running, and debugging Docker containers.
 CI/CD experience (GitHub Actions preferred) and exposure to Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform).
 Exposure to asynchronous and job-queue patterns (Redis/RQ, Celery, SQS) or background worker services.
 TypeScript and React experience, useful as the role broadens across the stack.
 Experience working directly with users or product partners to shape what gets built.
 Exposure to pharma, clinical, regulatory, or pharmacovigilance data, or to CDISC/SDTM, TLFs, or clinical study reports. Not required — we will teach the domain.
 Experience working in Agile methodology in GxP or other highly regulated environments.
 
 Required Skills: 
Agile Project Management, Amazon Web Services (AWS), API Development, Biopharmaceuticals, Computer Engineering, Data Engineering, Data Modeling, Design Applications, Docker Container, Generative AI, GitHub Actions, Large Language Models (LLMs), Software Configurations, Software Development, Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), Solution Architecture, TypeScript
